The adjective is derived partly from the following: * Etymology 1, adjective sense 1: Middle English crisp (“curly, wavy”), from Old English crisp (“curly”), from Latin crispus (“of hair: crimped, curly”), possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kris-, from *(s)ker- (“to bend; to turn”). * Etymology 1, adjective sense 2: from the above, and probably also onomatopoeic, representing a crinkling or crunching sound. Doublet of crape and crepe.

chain.g: to curl; of hair: to be curly

ety.text: Partly from the following: * Etymology 2 sense 1: crisp (adjective; see etymology 1). * Etymology 2 sense 2: Late Middle English crispen (“to curl; of hair: to be curly”), from Old English cirpsian (“to curl, crisp”), from Latin crīspō (“to crimp; to curl”), from crispus (“of hair: crimped, curly”, adjective) (see etymology 1) + -ō (suffix forming infinitives of first-conjugation verbs).

senses.d: Of hair: curling, especially in tight, stiff curls or ringlets; also (obsolete), of a person: having hair curled in this manner.
ex: crisp hair
A certeyn lightning on his headtop gliſtered harmeleſſe. / His criſp locks frizeling, his temples prettelye ſtroaking.

senses.d: Of a body of water, skin, etc.: having a surface which is rippled or wrinkled.
ex: The elder ladies' wrinkles curled much crisper / As they beheld; […]
[T]here was a fresh smell of seaweed, and the tiny ripples curled crisp and white along the pebbly bays.

senses.d: Synonym of crispate (“of a leaf: having curled, notched, or wavy edges”); crisped.
ex: Feathered VVater Moſs. Branched. Leaves criſp, feathered, undulated, pointing tvvo vvays.

senses.d: Clear; also, shining, or smooth.
ex: […] Fryer, you muſt leave / Your neat criſpe Clarret, and fall to your Syder / Avvhile; […]

senses.d: Having a consistency which is hard yet brittle, and in a condition to break with a sharp fracture; crumbly, friable, short.
ex: The crisp snow crunched underfoot.
Our customers in the produce department expect crisp apples and firm bananas.

senses.d: Not limp; firm, stiff; not stale or wilted; fresh; also, effervescent, lively.
ex: A crisp fresh odour of starch wafted from the cardboard-stiff jacket which covered a well-built, Sunday athlete's frame.

senses.d: Of action, movement, a person's manner, etc.: precise and quick; brisk.
ex: An expert, given a certain query, will often come up with a crisp answer: “yes” or “no”.
A very estimable young person, Miss Sturch […] such a well-regulated mind, and such a crisp touch on the piano; […]

senses.d: Of air, weather, etc.: cool and dry; also, of a period of time: characterized by such weather.
Of fabric, paper, etc.: clean and uncreased.
Of something heard or seen: clearly defined; clean, neat, sharp.
ex: This new television set has a very crisp image.

senses.d: In full potato crisp: a thin slice of potato which has been deep-fried until it is brittle and crispy, and eaten when cool; they are typically packaged and sold as a snack.
ex: Edward, give me another of those delicious olives. / What's that? Potato crisps? No, I can't endure them.
Turn you inside out and lick you like a crisp packet

senses.d: Sometimes with a descriptive word: a crispy, savoury snack made of some other ingredient(s) (such as cornmeal or a vegetable) which is baked or deep-fried and eaten like a potato crisp.
ex: kale crisps    prawn crisp

senses.d: A type of baked dessert consisting of fruit topped with a crumbly mixture made with fat, flour, and sugar; a crumble.
A banknote; also, a number of banknotes collectively.
Chiefly in to a crisp: a food item that has been overcooked, or a thing which has been burned, to the point of becoming charred or dried out.
The crispy rind of roast pork; crackling.
A curly lock of hair, especially one which is tightly curled.
ex: They are proud, and vveare their hayre pretty long, and about their criſpes vvreath a valuable Shaſh or Tulipant; […]

senses.d: A delicate fabric, possibly resembling crepe, especially used by women for veils or other head coverings in the past; also, a head covering made of this fabric.
ex: Vpon her head a ſiluer criſp ſhe pind, / Looſe vvauing on her ſhoulders vvith the vvind.
[T]he nevv deuiſed names of Stuffes and Colours, Crispe, Tamet, Pluſh, Tabine, Caffa, […]

senses.d: To make (something) firm yet brittle; specifically (cooking), to give (food) a crispy surface through frying, grilling, or roasting.
ex: to crisp bacon by frying it

senses.d: To add small amounts of colour to (something); to tinge, to tint.
ex: It was the form of a man of middle age, the hair white, but the beard only crisped with grey,
The leaves of the chestnut were crisped with gold.

senses.d: To become firm yet brittle; specifically (cooking), of food: to form a crispy surface through frying, grilling, or roasting.
ex: to put celery into ice water to crisp
The dew is dried that drenched our hide / Or washed about our way; / And where we drank, the puddled bank / Is crisping into clay.

senses.d: To make a sharp crackling or crunching sound.
ex: […] everything had become so still that the crisping of the snow under foot might be heard nearly half a verst round.
[…] the wheels [of the carriage] made their little crisping over the fine metal of the driveway.

senses.d: To curl (something, such as fabric) into tight, stiff folds or waves; to crimp, to crinkle; specifically, to form (hair) into tight curls or ringlets.
ex:
1609, Douay-Rheims Bible, 2 Chronicles 4.5,
[…] the brimme therof was as it were the brimme of a chalice, or of a crisped lilie:
[…] those crisped snaky golden locks / Which make such wanton gambols with the wind,

senses.d: To cause (a body of water) to undulate irregularly; to ripple.
ex: […] the crisped Brooks, / Rowling on Orient Pearl and sands of Gold
[…] when the breeze crisps the pool, you may see the image of the breakers, and a likeness of the foam.

senses.d: To twist or wrinkle (a body part).
ex: They were not the ordinary pyramid-shaped teeth of most sharks. They were shaped like a man's fingers when they are crisped like claws.

senses.d: To fold (newly woven cloth).
To become curled into tight, stiff folds or waves.
ex: […] a few shreds of purple bloom on a brown, crisping tuft of self-heal

senses.d: Of a body of water: to ripple, to undulate.
ex: […] the quick yielding of the waves that crisp and curl and ripple about my body.
